title: AI thermal-camera early warning stops trains for elephants at Madukkarai, Tamil Nadu
summary: TN Forest Dept AI cameras on a 7.05 km rail stretch: 7,116+ alerts, thousands of train stops, zero elephant deaths since Feb 2024.
account: The Tamil Nadu Forest Department installed 24 hybrid thermal cameras with AI detection on 12 towers along 7.05 km of the Ettimadai–Walayar railway section in Madukkarai forest range, Coimbatore district, operating since 9 February 2024 after a trial run that was already generating alerts by 7 January 2024. Alerts go to a control room at Puthupathi, whose staff warn station masters and loco pilots and drive elephants away from the tracks. By 7 July 2026 the department's Additional Chief Secretary reported more than 7,116 alerts, 3,281 (DT Next reports 3,821) instances of trains slowing or stopping, about 9,481 safe elephant crossings and no elephant deaths on the stretch, where eleven elephants were killed between 2008 and 2022.
purpose: Detect elephants near railway tracks with thermal cameras and AI, alert forest staff and railway crews, and prevent train-elephant collisions.
system: AI-based elephant early warning system (24 hybrid thermal cameras on 12 towers, Elephant Control and Command Centre, Puthupathi)
deployer: Tamil Nadu Forest Department (Department of Environment, Climate Change and Forests), with railway station masters at Walayar and Ettimadai and loco pilots

ratings.reason: Unassessed: the reports count train stops and crossings, not injuries avoided by crews or passengers.
The Forest Department reports zero elephant deaths on a stretch that recorded eleven deaths from 2008 to 2022, including three in November 2021.

Reported 9,481 safe crossings and no track deaths for wild elephants on a stretch that recorded eleven deaths from 2008 to 2022; counterfactual per crossing is unproven, so not rated population-level.

ai_role.statement: AI classification of thermal-camera feeds generated the alerts that triggered staff intervention and train slow-downs; the department's figures (alerts, stops, crossings, zero deaths) are the department's own statements as reproduced verbatim in news reports, not an official document fetched directly, and no per-event counterfactual is established.
